findings.title: Cleanup deletes expired reminders for every method
findings.body: The first `OR` branch retains the previous `method: SMS` condition, but the new `retryCount > 1` branch does not. As a result, every workflow reminder of any method—including email and WhatsApp reminders—is deleted by this SMS cron once its retry count exceeds 1. Scope this branch to SMS (or otherwise ensure this cleanup cannot remove other reminder types), so this endpoint does not destroy unrelated reminders.

findings.title: Retries stop after the first failure
findings.body: When `scheduleSMS` returns `false`, this increments `retryCount` but leaves `scheduled` false. On the next cron run, the reminder is selected again, but this branch deletes reminders only when `retryCount > 1`; the second failed attempt raises the count to 2, and the reminder is not deleted until a later cron run. This means the described two-attempt limit is not enforced immediately and leaves a failed reminder in the database for at least one extra run. Delete it when the second attempt fails, or align the cleanup threshold and behavior.

findings.title: Retry increments can be lost across overlapping cron runs
findings.body: Each run reads `retryCount` and later writes `reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two cron invocations process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both can read the same count and write the same increment; the reminder is then retried more times than the configured limit. Use an atomic increment and claim/lock reminders before scheduling, so concurrent runs cannot lose increments or duplicate scheduling attempts.
